title: Static methods written in the AeroTopo project
answer: Yes. AeroTopo uses static methods where behavior has no need for per-instance state. `SurveyAlgorithms` exposes static methods for array, String, numeric, and search algorithms, and `LanguageLab` has static utilities such as `sum` and `numericConversions`. These methods operate only on parameters or class-level state. In project code I would keep behavior instance-based when it depends on injected collaborators, configuration, or mutable object state.
